A [@scope](CSS-CASCADE-6#at-ruledef-scope) rule produces one or more [scopes](CSS-CASCADE-6#scope) as follows: Finding the [scoping root](SELECTORS-4#scoping-root)(s) For each element matched by [\](CSS-CASCADE-6#typedef-scope-start), create a [scope](CSS-CASCADE-6#scope) using that element as the [scoping root](SELECTORS-4#scoping-root). If no \ is specified, the scoping root is the [parent element](DOM#parent-element) of the [owner node](CSSOM-1#cssstyledeclaration-owner-node) of the stylesheet where the [@scope](CSS-CASCADE-6#at-ruledef-scope) rule is defined. (If no such element exists and the containing [node tree](DOM#concept-node-tree) is a [shadow tree](DOM#concept-shadow-tree), then the scoping root is the shadow host. Otherwise, the scoping root is the [root](DOM#concept-tree-root) of the containing node tree.) Any [:scope](SELECTORS-4#scope-pseudo) or [&](CSS-NESTING-1#selectordef-) selectors in \ are interpreted as defined for its outer context. Finding any [scoping limits](CSS-CASCADE-6#scoping-limit) For each [scope](CSS-CASCADE-6#scope) created by a [scoping root](SELECTORS-4#scoping-root), its [scoping limits](CSS-CASCADE-6#scoping-limit) are set to all elements that are [descendants](DOM#concept-tree-descendant) of the scoping root and that match [\](CSS-CASCADE-6#typedef-scope-end), interpreting [:scope](SELECTORS-4#scope-pseudo) and [&](CSS-NESTING-1#selectordef-) exactly as in [scoped style rules](CSS-CASCADE-6#scoped-style-rules). > **Example:** Authors can establish local scoping for [`style`](HTML#the-style-element) elements by leaving out the [\](CSS-CASCADE-6#typedef-scope-start) selector. For example: > > ``` >
> >

this is red

>
>

not red

> ``` > > That would be equivalent to: > > ``` >
> >

this is red

>
>

not red

> ``` > **Example:** [Scoping limits](CSS-CASCADE-6#scoping-limit) can use the [:scope](SELECTORS-4#scope-pseudo) pseudo-class to require a specific relationship to the [scoping root](SELECTORS-4#scoping-root): > > ``` > /* .content is only a limit when it is a direct child of the :scope */ > @scope (.media-object) to (:scope > .content) { ... } > ``` > > [Scoping limits](CSS-CASCADE-6#scoping-limit) can also reference elements outside their [scoping root](SELECTORS-4#scoping-root) by using [:scope](SELECTORS-4#scope-pseudo). For example: > > ``` > /* .content is only a limit when the :scope is inside .sidebar */ > @scope (.media-object) to (.sidebar :scope .content) { ... } > ```
title: Identifying Scoping Roots and Limits
